newsitem.title: UK: S&P assigns new criteria for rating pfandbriefe.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns new criteria for rating pfandbriefe.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it had developed new criteria for rating pfandbriefe, a special type of collateralised bond issued by German banks, which allowed them to exceed the banks' counterparty ratings.
"Outstanding pfandbriefe total about 1.4 trillion marks ($897 billion), representing more than one-third of the German bond market," S&P said.
"Their collateral, coupled with protections afforded by German insovency and banking laws, permit S&P to rate some pfandbriefe above the bank's counterparty rating."
S&P said the new criteria are currently applicable to private-sector German mortgage and mixed mortgage banks.

"Although such institutions are subject to the risk of failure, S&P believes that holders of some pfandbriefe, especially those backed by public sector loans, may continue to receive full and timely payments in the event of the bank's insolvency," S&P said.
It said analysis of the specific collateral was key to the rating decision.

"Achievement of a rating significantly above the bank's counterparty rating may require registration of more collateral than the minumum level required by banking regulations. Pfandbriefe backed by sufficient high-quality collateral could earn a AAA rating, regardless of the bank's counterparty rating," S&P said.
